title: Solo indie dev here. My game runs entirely on physics: ragdoll helpers and a golem boss with zero animations
author: No-Cow3446
selftext:
Hi! I'm an indie developer working solo on a Unity game. The hero has a squad of small ragdoll creatures you command, even with your voice. They stack into a pyramid, link into a living bridge across a gap, pull a chain, and you can gather them into a ball of light and hurl them. No canned animations: everything is simulated, so it plays out a little differently every time.

The golem scene in the crystal cave. The golem is a ragdoll too, driven by muscle forces, so it can genuinely trip, fall and get back up. Its brain runs on an "enemy file": moves scored by the situation, fight phases and a memory of what the player did in the last ten seconds. It throws rocks with lead, vanishes into fog and comes out behind you, pounds the wall so debris rains from the ceiling, and sometimes melts into lava that flows toward your helpers and shoots fireballs from the puddle.

Any feedback is welcome.
